newsitem.title: INDONESIA: First ASEAN business summit to be held this week.
newsitem.headline: First ASEAN business summit to be held this week.

text.p: Business leaders from the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) and its trading partners will meet in Jakarta this week to discuss trade and investment flows to the region, organisers said on Monday.

The two-day ASEAN Business Summit, the first meeting of its kind, will be inaugurated by Indonesian President Suharto on Wednesday, they said. Some 600 delegates, including more than 100 from the United States, are expected to attend.

"The private sector is the engine of growth, the government is the facilitator," said ASEAN Chambers of Commerce and Industry secretary-general Setyanto Santosa. "The private sector feels it is necessary for top executives of companies to meet together."

Participants will include Thai Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viravan, Malaysian Trade Minister Rafidah Aziz, Singapore Trade and Industry Minister Lee Yock Suan, Philippine Trade Secretary Cesar Bautista, United Technologies president George David, Singapore Airlines chairman S. Dhanabalan and former U.S. Secretary of State Alexander Haig.

The seven ASEAN nations -- Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam -- will give presentations on trade and investment opportunities in their countries, organisers said.

ASEAN Chambers of Commerce president Aburizal Bakrie has said the investment environment in the Philippines could be one area of focus because of a Philippine Supreme Court decision that overturned the sale of the government-owned Manila hotel to a Malaysian firm and awarded it to a local company under a "Filipino First" policy.

Economists have said the decision could be a setback to Manila's efforts to privatise state industries, the cornerstone of its economic reform programme. President Fidel Ramos has said the Philippine government will consider amending the constitution to block courts from halting the reforms.

Indonesia's automobile policy, which grants a company controlled by Suharto's son, Hutomo Mandala Putra, tax and tariff breaks to build a national car, could also come under scrutiny, participants said.
ASEAN and U.S. businessmen would hold a separate conclave during the summit, they added.

"This delegation is the largest delegation of private businessmen from the United States to visit Indonesia," said Arian Ardie, deputy secretary general of the U.S. committee of Kadin, the Indonesian chambers of commerce.
He said continuing deregulation and privatisation in ASEAN in the energy, oil and gas sectors would be of interest to the U.S. delegation as would the continuing promotion of small-scale businesses.
